sentences.text: 2  JUDGMENT Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for respondent No.2 and perused the material on record.

2. This appeal is preferred by the claimants in MVC No.1555/2019 on the file of the MACT-XV,
Vijayapura, (for short 'the tribunal') wherein, vide judgment and award dated 18.01.2022, the claimants are awarded a total compensation of Rs.20,88,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization, for the death of one Vilas Chavan in a road traffic accident which took place on 06.09.2019 at about 3.45 p.m., near Jai Karnataka Dhaba, Kapa-Nimbaragi cross, on NH-13 road.

According to the claimants, at the time of accident, the deceased was riding a motorcycle bearing registration No.MH-42/U-1324 and a car bearing registration No.MH- 13/DE-2425 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner came from Solapur side and hit against the NC: 2023:KHC-K:7350-DB motorcycle, due to which he sustained fatal injuries and died.
3.
The claimants are the parents, wife and four minor children of the deceased.

Before the tribunal,
PWs.1 to 3 were examined on behalf of the claimants and Exs.P1 to P7 were marked.
The respondents got marked Ex.R1- Insurance Policy, however did not examine any witnesses.
The contention of respondent No.2/Insurance Company was that the accident was solely due to the rash and negligent riding by the deceased.

4. The tribunal on appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence on record, held that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the car and hence answered issue Nos.1 and 2 in the affirmative and issue No.4 in the negative.

5. Insofar as the findings recorded by the tribunal holding that the accident was on account of negligence of the driver of the car which was insured with respondent NC: 2023:KHC-K:7350-DB No.2 is concerned, the same has become final.

The tribunal awarded compensation under the following heads:
 Sl.No. Heads By Tribunal  1. Loss of dependency Rs.19,08,000/-
 2. Loss of consortium Rs.50,000/-

3 . Loss of filial love and Rs.1,00,000/-
 affection  4. Funeral expenses and Rs.20,000/-
 obsequies  5. Loss of estate Rs.10,000/-
 Total Rs.20,88,000/-

sentences.text: The accident took place on 06.09.2019.
The income, age of the deceased, multiplier taken by the tribunal is not seriously disputed by the learned counsel for the appellants.
He would contend that the tribunal has erred in not considering the future prospects while calculating the amount under the head "loss of dependency".
7. On perusal of the impugned judgment, we find that the tribunal has not considered the future prospects while calculating the compensation under the head loss of NC: 2023:KHC-K:7350-DB dependency.
The deceased was aged about 37 years at the time of accident.
His income having rightly assessed at Rs.13,250/-, another sum of Rs.5,300/- which is 40% of the said amount, has to be added to the income towards future prospects.
Hence, the claimants are entitled for a sum of Rs.26,71,200/- (Rs.13,250 + 5,300 = Rs.18,550/- x 4/5 x 12 x 15) towards loss of dependency.

8. The learned counsel for the appellants has contended that there are seven claimants, who are the parents, wife and four children of the deceased and therefore, the Tribunal was not justified in not awarding just compensation under the parental and filial consortium, on the other hand, awarded only a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- towards loss of consortium and loss of filial love and affection.
9.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of New India Assurance Company Limited vs. Somwati and others1 has held that the expression "consortium" includes (2020) 9 SCC 644 NC:
2023:KHC-K:7350-DB spousal consortium, parental consortium as well as filial consortium.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Limited vs. Somwati and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Apart from spousal consortium, parental and filial consortium are payable in fatal accident claim.
10. In the light of the above judgment, we deem it proper to award a sum of Rs.2,80,000/- towards spousal/ parental/filial consortium.
A sum of Rs.30,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards funeral expenses and loss of estate is unaltered.
Hence, the claimants are entitled for a total compensation of Rs.29,81,200/- as against Rs.20,88,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is partly allowed.
(ii) The judgment and award dated 18.01.2022 passed in MVC No.1555/2019 by the Court of Motor Accident Claims Tribunal NO.XV, Vijayapura, is modified.

NC: 2023:KHC-K:7350-DB awarded by the Tribunal, with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
(iii) Respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
(iv) Rest of the judgment passed by the Tribunal is not disturbed.
